officialTitle: Lenvatinib in patients with advanced or metastatic thymic carcinoma (REMORA): a multicentre, phase 2 trial
setting: Advanced or metastatic thymic carcinoma after platinum-based chemotherapy

design.blinding: Open-label; ORR by independent central review
design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between April 21, 2017, and Feb 22, 2018, 42 patients were enrolled and all patients were included in the activity and safety analysis.
design.notes: Single-arm, multicentre phase 2 trial in eight Japanese institutions. Non-comparative evidence.

sponsor: Center for Clinical Trials, Japan Medical Association
clinicalQuestion: What is the activity and safety of lenvatinib as second-line treatment for advanced or metastatic thymic carcinoma?

pico.population: Unresectable advanced or metastatic thymic carcinoma progressing after at least one platinum-based chemotherapy, ECOG PS 0-1
pico.outcomes: Primary: ORR by independent central review (ITT). Safety

arms.label: Lenvatinib
arms.dosing: 24 mg orally once daily in 4-week cycles
arms.doseSourceQuote: Patients received 24 mg of lenvatinib orally once daily in 4-week cycles until disease progression or occurrence of unacceptable adverse events.

publications.title: Lenvatinib in patients with advanced or metastatic thymic carcinoma (REMORA): a multicentre, phase 2 trial.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: The objective response rate was 38% (90% CI 25·6-52·0, p<0·0001). 16 (38%) of 42 patients had a partial response and 24 (57%) had stable disease.

safety.sourceQuote: The most frequent grade 3 treatment-related adverse events were hypertension (27 [64%]) and palmar-plantar erythrodysaesthesia syndrome (three [7%]). No patient died from adverse events.
No patient died from adverse events.

strengths: Multicentre prospective trial with independent central review of response
Intention-to-treat analysis of all enrolled patients
limitations: Single-arm phase II evidence; no comparator
High rate of grade 3 hypertension requiring active management

clinicalImplications.text: Single-arm phase II data supporting lenvatinib as an active second-line option in thymic carcinoma, with hypertension as the dominant toxicity.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Plan blood-pressure monitoring and early antihypertensive therapy when starting lenvatinib for thymic carcinoma.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 32502444. Registry JMA-IIA00285 is the JMACCT registry as printed.
